synthetic_negative_controls: A one-second budget expires during T setup, preserves completed setup streams and prevents the provider CLI launch.
A one-second budget expires during the provider CLI before its per-stage timeout and preserves the raw CLI stream.
Expiry before T post-CLI status prevents that subprocess from launching; expiry during status retains its partial capture.
A forged ready status contradicted by a captured CLI timeout is rejected by the observer.
A forged total elapsed shorter than the sum of verified setup, CLI and T status capture durations is rejected.
A timed-out child that responds to SIGTERM and one with a resistant descendant are signalled while the process-group leader is still reserved, before reaping.

initial_findings: The observer accepted a ready status with total elapsed shorter than a captured CLI duration.
The timeout handler sent SIGKILL after the process-group leader had already been reaped.
independent_read_only_review.recheck: Both local inconsistencies were reproduced, corrected and rechecked with fake CLIs; the elapsed forgery now exits 2 and the second group signal precedes reaping.
independent_read_only_review.remaining_counterexample: A same-UID writer can rewrite unsealed run.json after post_cli expiry (or remove new fields to mimic a legacy run) and make the local observer report artifacts_ready_for_inspection; no independent capture proves the post-CLI delay. Coherent rewriting of wall_seconds can also evade the local sum.
